description: A rebuild of a mechanical rehearsal metronome: a dial of the 39 traditional tempo marks, and a jack that pulses on the beat

params.text: Sets the tempo, moving between the 39 marks around the dial
Sets the tempo to the mark beside it and clears whichever mark was set before
Sets the tempo the reset jack returns to, chosen from the same 39 marks

inputs.text: A rising edge moves three marks faster, wrapping round to the slowest end past 208
A rising edge moves two marks faster, wrapping round to the slowest end past 208
A rising edge moves one mark faster, wrapping round to 40 past 208
A rising edge moves one mark slower, wrapping round to 208 past 42; 40 is never reached this way
A rising edge sets the tempo to the mark held by the reset tempo knob
A rising edge starts the metronome, or stops it and clears the count

outputs.text: A 10V pulse one millisecond long on every beat, starting the moment the metronome is started

notes: nothing is counted until the output is patched: the clock only advances while a cable is in the impulse out jack and the start button is on.
the marks are the traditional metronome numbers, 40 to 60 in twos, 60 to 72 in threes, 72 to 96 in fours, 96 to 120 in fours, then 126 to 144 in sixes and on to 208 in eights.
